diagnosis.bottleneck: The query performs two full sequential scans of the same 'trips' table (reading all columns to evaluate filters, though only three are projected) and then hash-deduplicates the combined ~198k rows via HASH_GROUP_BY.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)
HASH_GROUP_BY deduplicates on all three columns; if the two result sets have little overlap, replacing UNION with UNION ALL (and accepting duplicates) would eliminate the hash aggregation entirely.

Each SEQ_SCAN reads full rows despite projecting only three columns; a covering index on (trip_distance, fare_amount) INCLUDE (PULocationID, payment_type, passenger_count) could enable index-only scans for both predicates.
